# Production brief: Nobody Knows My Name Here

## Tempo map

Constant 118 bpm, 4/4, straight eighths throughout. No tempo changes; a one-bar drum break at the end of the Bridge leads into the final Chorus. Count-in of one bar on closed hi-hat.

## Vocal treatment

Dry single lead in the verses with a short plate reverb (0.8 s decay, 20 ms pre-delay). Pre-choruses add a tight stereo double. Choruses use lead plus two stereo doubles and a 1/8-note slap delay at roughly 15 percent wet. Final Chorus adds a group vocal on the hook line only, panned wide and low-passed at 8 kHz. Light de-essing on every lead track; compression at 4:1 with a slow attack so consonants stay forward.

## Mix priorities

1. Lead vocal intelligibility on the hook line.
2. Kick and bass locked; sidechain the pad lightly to the kick in the choruses.
3. Acoustic guitar carries the verses, so keep its 2-4 kHz body; cut the same band on the synth pad.
4. Keep the Bridge noticeably quieter (about 4 dB) so the final Chorus lands.

## Section notes

- Verse 1: guitar and bass only, hi-hat enters bar 5.
- Pre-Chorus 1: kick and snare enter, bass walks up to the Chorus root.
- Chorus: full kit, pad, doubled vocal; hi-hat half open.
- Verse 2: drop the pad, add shaker, keep the kit but at a lower velocity.
- Pre-Chorus 2: tambourine and backing vocals on the second line, tom fill into the Chorus.
- Bridge: piano and voice, bass enters at bar 5, drum break on bar 8.
- Final Chorus: everything in, open hi-hat, group vocal on the hook.
